rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a Day-5 expanded blastocyst and acknowledges possible handling-related collapse, but it over-interprets image details (e.g., focal opening/hatching side, exact ICM cell count) and questions the reported BA grade without strong visual basis.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, BMI, semen quality, lining, and lack of prior failures well, and relates these factors to prognosis, though some interactions are discussed somewhat broadly.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical: good age/lining/semen improve prognosis while endometriosis and non-elite morphology temper expectations. Minor issues include speculative morphology and somewhat broad probability framing.

Mostly aligned with IVF practice: respects Gardner grading, supports single embryo transfer in a very young patient, and does not overstate PGT-A. Small deviations include speculative comments about laparoscopy and some nonessential lifestyle advice.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and future evaluation, including SET, luteal support, cavity assessment if failures occur, and endometriosis-focused planning. Recommendations are useful, though not highly protocol-specific.
